intro_en: This is the last lesson of your N5 journey. You will learn 〜たら, for "if" ("if it rains tomorrow"). You will learn 〜ても, for "even if" ("even if it rains"). You will also learn いくら〜ても ("no matter how hard I try"), つもり ("I plan to") and 予定 ("a plan / schedule"). They work just like the Tamil verb endings "-ஆல்" (if) and "-ஆலும்" (even if). So they should feel easy. At the end, we look back at the forms you have learned: the て, ない, dictionary and た forms. You will see a full map of what each one does.

g25-1.explanation_en: Add ら to the た-form from Lesson 19. Then you get the "if" form: 降った → 降ったら (if it rains). It has two meanings. (1) "If, by chance, ... happens": 雨が降ったら、行きません (if it rains, I won’t go). (2) "After something that will surely happen is finished": 駅に着いたら、電話してください (when you arrive at the station, please call me). It matches the Tamil endings exactly: "-ஆல்" (if) and "-ஆனதும்" (as soon as). For "not": 〜なかったら (if ... doesn’t come / happen). い-adjectives: 安かったら. な-adjectives and nouns: 暇だったら、雨だったら. と from Lesson 23 is different. After たら, you can say a wish, an order or an invitation: 〜たら、〜てください / 〜ましょう / 〜たいです. That is why たら is the most useful "if" in everyday talk.
g25-1.tamil_parallel_en: "மழை பெய்தால் போகமாட்டேன்" (if it rains, I won’t go) = 雨が降ったら、行きません ； "ஸ்டேஷனை அடைந்ததும் போன் செய்யுங்கள்" (when you reach the station, please call) = 駅に着いたら、電話してください. Tamil "-ஆல்" ("பெய்தால்") and "-ஆனதும்" ("அடைந்ததும்") are both covered by たら.
g25-1.formation_en: Verb た-form + ら ； verb なかった + ら ； い-adjective かった + ら ； な-adjective / noun + だった + ら
g25-1.pitfalls_en: Putting the dictionary form before たら is wrong: ×降るたら → ○降ったら. Nouns need だった: ×雨たら → ○雨だったら.

g25-2.explanation_en: "Even if it rains, I will go." Here the result is not what you would expect. For this, use て-form + も. It matches Tamil "-ஆலும்" exactly ("பெய்தாலும்" even if it rains, "சாப்பிட்டாலும்" even if I eat). Look: Tamil "உம்" and Japanese も both mean "even / also"! 降って → 降っても、食べて → 食べても. い-adjectives: 高い → 高くても (even if it is expensive). な-adjectives and nouns: 暇 → 暇でも、雨 → 雨でも. For "not": 〜なくても. You saw this form in なくてもいいです in Lesson 17. 〜てもいいですか (may I do it?) from Lesson 15 also comes from this form. It means "is it all right even if I do it?"
g25-2.tamil_parallel_en: "மழை பெய்தாலும் போவேன்" (even if it rains, I will go) = 雨が降っても、行きます. て-form + も = Tamil "-ஆலும்". Both も and "உம்" have the meaning "even".
g25-2.formation_en: Verb て-form + も ； verb なくて + も ； い-adjective くて + も ； な-adjective / noun + でも
g25-2.pitfalls_en: For an い-adjective, 高いでも is wrong: ○高くても. Don’t mix up 〜ても and 〜たら. ても = "even if" (a result you don’t expect). たら = "if" (a natural result).

g25-3.explanation_en: These two are helper words at the start of a sentence. They tell the listener early which form is coming later. (1) もし + 〜たら: it makes the "if" stronger, "if by chance": もし雨が降ったら (if by chance it rains). It matches Tamil "ஒருவேளை" (perhaps / if by chance). Without もし, the meaning is the same. But with it, the listener knows from the start that an "if" is coming. (2) いくら + 〜ても: "no matter how much ...". In Lesson 3, you learned いくら as "how much (price)". With ても, it means "however much": いくら勉強しても、漢字は難しいです. It matches Tamil "எவ்வளவு படித்தாலும்" (no matter how much I study) exactly. After いくら, always use ても (not たら).
g25-3.tamil_parallel_en: "ஒருவேளை மழை பெய்தால்" (if by chance it rains) = もし雨が降ったら ； "எவ்வளவு படித்தாலும்" (no matter how much I study) = いくら勉強しても. Tamil "ஒருவேளை" matches もし. Tamil "எவ்வளவு ... -ஆலும்" matches いくら ... ても.
g25-3.formation_en: もし + 〜たら、〜 ； いくら + verb て-form / い-adjective くて / noun で + も、〜
g25-3.pitfalls_en: ×いくら勉強したら is wrong. いくら only goes with ても. After もし, the natural form is 〜たら, not 〜ても.

g25-4.explanation_en: To talk about something you have decided in your mind, use dictionary form + つもりです: 来年日本へ行くつもりです (I plan to go to Japan next year). It matches Tamil "போக எண்ணியிருக்கிறேன்" (I intend to go). It also matches "போகலாம் என்று இருக்கிறேன்" (I’m thinking of going). For "plan not to do", use ない-form + つもりです: たばこを吸わないつもりです. つもり is a noun. So the "sentence + noun" rule from Lesson 22 works here. 〜たいです from Lesson 13 is only a wish. つもり is something you have decided. Be careful with a boss or an older person. Asking them "what do you plan to do?" with つもりですか can sound a little rude.
g25-4.tamil_parallel_en: "அடுத்த ஆண்டு ஜப்பான் போக எண்ணியிருக்கிறேன்" (I intend to go to Japan next year) = 来年日本へ行くつもりです. The Tamil "to" form + "எண்ணியிருக்கிறேன்" (I have in mind) matches dictionary form + つもりです.
g25-4.formation_en: Verb dictionary form + つもりです ； verb ない-form + つもりです
g25-4.pitfalls_en: The ます-form and たい do not come before つもり: ×行きますつもり、×行きたいつもり → ○行くつもり.

g25-5.explanation_en: 予定 (よてい) means "plan, schedule". つもり is a plan in your mind. 予定 is a fixed event. It is written on the calendar, and other people know about it. Dictionary form + 予定です: 来月結婚する予定です (the wedding is planned for next month). Noun + の + 予定です: 旅行の予定です. You also use it for schedules you don’t control, like trains, flights and meetings: 電車は十時に着く予定です. It matches Tamil "திட்டம்" (plan) and "ஏற்பாடு" (arrangement). "Do you have any plans?" = 何か予定がありますか.
g25-5.tamil_parallel_en: "அடுத்த மாதம் திருமணம் நடக்கத் திட்டம்" (the wedding is planned for next month) = 来月結婚する予定です ； "நாளை மறுநாள் பயணத் திட்டம்" (the day after tomorrow, I have a trip planned) = 明後日は旅行の予定です. Tamil "திட்டம்" (plan) comes after a verb or noun. It works like 予定.
g25-5.formation_en: Verb dictionary form + 予定です ； noun + の + 予定です ； 予定が あります
g25-5.pitfalls_en: Don’t forget の after a noun: ×旅行予定です → ○旅行の予定です. You sometimes hear ×旅行予定です when people talk. But for N5, use の.

g25-6.explanation_en: In N5 you learned five forms of a verb. Let’s see what each one does, all in one place. We use 行く as the example. ① ます-form (行きます): the polite sentence ending. Its stem (行き, the part before ます) + たい (wish), ながら (while), ましょう/ましょうか, に行く (go to do). ② て-form (行って): like the Tamil form "போய்" (having gone). It is used in てください (asking), ている (doing now / a state), てもいい (you may), てはいけない (you must not), てから (after), て、て (one after another), てあげる/くれる/もらう (doing favours), ても (even if). ③ ない-form (行かない): like Tamil "போகாத" (not going). It is used in ないでください (please don’t), なければなりません (must), なくてもいい (don’t have to), ないつもり. ④ Dictionary form (行く): ことができる (can), ことです (hobby), 前に (before), と (result that always follows), つもり, 予定, describing a noun (行く人), と思う, 時. ⑤ た-form (行った): たことがある (have done before), たり〜たり (listing), たほうがいい (advice), たあとで (after), たら (if), た時, 行った人 (describing a noun, past). Tamil also makes many forms from one verb: "போய்", "போகாத", "போகும்", "போன", "போனால்". It is just the same. In plain (casual) style (Lesson 20), forms ④, ⑤ and ③ can also end a sentence.
g25-6.tamil_parallel_en: "போய்" (having gone, て) / "போகாத" (not going, ない) / "போகும்" (that goes, dictionary) / "போன" (that went, た) / "போனால்" (if I go, たら) / "போனாலும்" (even if I go, ても) = 行って / 行かない / 行く / 行った / 行ったら / 行っても. Like Tamil, Japanese makes all these meanings from one verb. It just changes the ending.
g25-6.formation_en: ます-stem: たい・ながら・ましょう ； て: ください・いる・もいい・はいけない・から・あげる/くれる/もらう・も ； ない: でください・ければなりません・くてもいい ； dictionary form: ことができる・前に・と・つもり・予定・時・+ noun ； た: ことがある・り〜たり・ほうがいい・あとで・ら・時・+ noun
g25-6.pitfalls_en: To choose a form, look at what comes after it. Before ください, use て or ないで. Before ことがある, use た. Before ことができる, use the dictionary form. ×行くことがあります ≠ ○行ったことがあります. The first one has a different meaning: "I sometimes go". The second one means "I have gone there before".

items.L25-q01: 明後日 = あさって (நாளை மறுநாள், the day after tomorrow). This is a special reading. あさて is missing the small っ. みょうごにち is the formal form. In N5, only あさって is used.
items.L25-q02: 大学 = だいがく (பல்கலைக்கழகம், university). Here 大 is read だい, with the two dots. It is not たい, as in 大切 (たいせつ). That is the main trap. 学 is read がく in longer words.
items.L25-q03: 緑 = みどり (பச்சை, green). みとり has lost the dots. In Japan, あお (青) can sometimes mean green. But it is not the reading of this kanji.
items.L25-q04: らいげつ = 来月 (அடுத்த மாதம், next month). 来年 (らいねん) and 来週 (らいしゅう) sound different. 末 looks like 来, but it is a fake.
items.L25-q05: はんぶん = 半分 (பாதி, half). 反 (はん) is a different kanji with the same sound. 今 (いま) looks like 分. 羊 looks like 半, but it is a fake.
items.L25-q06: Time or money "takes / costs" = かかります (ஆகும், takes). あります would change the meaning to "there is one hour". なります means "becomes (changes)".
items.L25-q07: To say the exact time, use 丁度 (சரியாக, exactly). 多分 (probably) doesn’t fit a time you read from a clock. だんだん (little by little) and なかなか (not easily) don’t fit the meaning.
items.L25-q08: 外に (ほかに) = (வேறு, இதைத் தவிர, anything else / besides this). 全部に and 自分に make no sense here. The same kanji can also be read そと (outside). Choose the reading by the meaning.
items.L25-q09: 自分で = (தானே, சொந்தமாக, by oneself / on one’s own). 一人で means "alone" (without other people). The meaning is close. But to stress "my own room, by myself", use 自分で. 家庭で (at home) shows a place.
items.L25-q10: 色々な国 = (பல நாடுகள், various countries). 大切な (important) and 丈夫な (strong) are also な-adjectives. But they don’t fit with "food of the countries".
items.L25-q11: Five minutes past nine means it is "past" nine. So the answer is 九時すぎ (தாண்டி, past). 前 (before) is the exact opposite. 半 would mean half past nine. まで (until) makes no sense here. もう (already) also shows that the time has "passed".
items.L25-q12: さ来年 = (அடுத்த ஆண்டுக்கு அடுத்த ஆண்டு, the year after next) = 来年の次の年. つもり = a plan in your mind ≈ 〜たいと思っています. 来月 (next month) is the wrong time. 来年/去年 with the past form are wrong.
items.L25-q13: "No matter how long I waited, it didn’t come" = I waited a long time, but it didn’t come (வரவில்லை). The second choice says "it came after I waited a little". That is the exact opposite.
items.L25-q14: なくてもいい (தேவையில்லை, don’t have to) = 終わらなくても大丈夫 (முடியாவிட்டாலும் பரவாயில்லை, it’s fine even if it isn’t finished). The first choice, なければなりません (must), is the exact opposite. It is a common trap.
items.L25-q15: "If it rains, I won’t climb the mountain" = 降ったら (பெய்தால், if it rains). 降っても would mean "even if it rains, I won’t climb". That doesn’t make sense. 降るので means "because it will rain", as if it were sure.
items.L25-q16: Taking a walk even in the rain is not what you expect. So use 降っても (பெய்தாலும், even if it rains). 降ったら would mean "if it rains, I take a walk (because of the rain)". That sounds strange. 降る時 means "when it rains". It doesn’t fit with 毎朝 (every morning).
items.L25-q17: いくら always goes with ても: いくら練習しても (எவ்வளவு பயிற்சி செய்தாலும், no matter how much I practise) I don’t get good at kanji. いくら〜たら is a wrong mix. 練習すると means "if you practise (it always follows)". That goes against the meaning.
items.L25-q18: For a plan in your mind, use dictionary form + つもりです (எண்ணம், intention). 〜ほうです and 〜ことです are not used with this meaning. ことです is only used in the "my hobby is X" pattern.
items.L25-q19: Noun + の + 予定: 旅行の予定です (பயணத் திட்டம், a trip is planned). な is only for な-adjectives. With に, the link breaks, and it means "for the trip".
items.L25-q20: A request (〜てください) comes after it, so it must be たら: 着いたら (அடைந்ததும், when you arrive). A request cannot come after と (Lesson 23). That is the main trap.
items.L25-q21: い-adjective + ても = 広くても (விசாலமாக இருந்தாலும், even if it is spacious). 広いでも wrongly uses the な-adjective rule. 広くて would mean "because it is spacious". That goes against the meaning.
items.L25-q22: た-form + ことがあります = something you have done before (அனுபவம்) (Lesson 19). つもり and 予定 need the dictionary form before them, not the た-form.
items.L25-q23: もし お金が たくさん あったら、何を しますか。 — もし + the "if" part (〜たら) comes first. Then comes the question. あったら goes in the star position.
items.L25-q24: 大学を 出たら、日本の 会社で 働く つもりです。 — First the "if" part, then the place (日本の 会社で). At the end comes the dictionary form 働く + つもりです. 働く goes in the star position.
items.L25-q25: これは 母が 毎年 作って くれる お菓子です。 — (இது அம்மா ஒவ்வொரு ஆண்டும் செய்து தரும் இனிப்பு, these are the sweets my mother makes for me every year). The doer inside the describing part takes が (Lesson 22). てくれる (Lesson 24) describes the noun. 母が goes in the star position.
items.L25-q26: ［1］ "Even though I study every day, it is still hard." This is not what you expect, so use しても. ［2］ Use the dictionary form 働く + つもりです (a plan in your mind). 予定の is the wrong form. ［3］ もし + たら: "if by chance I make friends". A wish (〜たいです) comes after it, so と doesn’t fit.
